plan: [In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true private value is a weakly dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' strategies. No prior rounds exist to adjust behavior. Therefore I will bid my value of $14.0 (rounded to a $0.1 increment) to maximize long-run expected earnings.]

[With a private value of $34 and a second-price rule, truthful bidding is a dominant strategy. Other bidders are rational and values are independent; bidding my true value maximizes expected surplus: if I win I pay the second-highest bid, so bidding 34 secures positive payoff whenever competitors' highest bid is below 34. This is round 1 and values are redrawn independently, so no history to exploit. I will bid my value of 34.]

[This is a second-price (Vickrey) auction with independent private values. Truthful bidding (bid equal to my private value) is a weakly dominant strategy and maximizes expected long-run profit regardless of opponents' strategies. Ties are random; bids must be in $0.1 increments. I will bid my value, $33, to ensure optimal expected payoff.]
